title: Newton's law of universal gravitation
ced_evidence: 2.6.A.1: "inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the systems' centers of mass. Relevant equation: F_g = G m1 m2 / r^2"

control: explicitly excluded by the CED (2.6 BOUNDARY STATEMENT: AP Physics 1 does not expect students to know Kepler's first or second laws of planetary motion)
title: Kepler's first and second laws
body: The laws describing the shape of a planetary orbit and how orbital speed varies along it.

items.label: First law
items.meaning: planets move in ellipses with the Sun at one focus

items.label: Second law
items.meaning: a line from the Sun to the planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times

control: wrong owner topic (centripetal acceleration is topic 2.9, EK 2.9.A.1; 2.5 is Newton's second law)
title: Centripetal acceleration

control: reversed fact (CED 2.7.B.3: the coefficient of STATIC friction is typically greater than the coefficient of kinetic friction)
title: Comparing the coefficients of friction
body: The coefficient of kinetic friction is typically greater than the coefficient of static friction for a given pair of surfaces.

control: hook expansion contradicts the CED (2.7.A.1.ii: the force of friction does not depend on the size of the surface area of contact). The entry is correct, so only the hook should be rejected.
title: What the friction force does not depend on
body: The force of friction between two surfaces does not depend on the size of the surface area of contact.

expands_to.means: a larger contact area between the surfaces

hooks.when_to_use: when deciding what the friction force depends on
hooks.caution: State the dependence in CED terms when answering.

control: content from another unit (the work-energy theorem is Unit 3 work, energy and power, EK 3.2.A.4; it is not in the Unit 2 pages)
title: Work-energy theorem
body: The change in an object's kinetic energy is equal to the sum of the work done by all forces exerted on the object.
